newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian shares decline in 'normal correction'.
newsitem.headline: Russian shares decline in 'normal correction'.

text.p: Russian shares declined steadily on Monday in what brokers called a normal correction which was unrelated to news President Boris Yeltsin had postponed a trip to the Netherlands.
Towards the close at 1500 GMT, Mosenergo had fallen to $1.46 from $1.56 at Friday's close. UES fell to $0.1510 from $0.1575 and Rostelekom eased to $3.29 from $3.31.

"There was no panic. There was a critical mass who decided to take profits, but it happened slowly over a period of time," said Renaissance Capital trader Oleg Tatkov, who added that Russian operators had led profit-taking.
Traders said that profit-taking had been relatively light, especially on the part of Western clients, from whom orders had slowed down but not dried up.
"Without active Western buying, it is difficult for the Russian participants to support the market," Bank Menatep's Sergei Kosynkin said.
But operators have anticipated a correction for weeks and say the market has generally established a new trading level.
Many expect the correction to be over by midweek.
"This has been an opportunity to buy some cheaper stock," said Pavel Gronbjerg, co-head of equity trading at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
